facts.raw_span: A 61-year-old African American woman
bilateral knee osteoarthritis
acute bilateral knee swelling and pain, left greater than right
denied fever, chills, or malaise
right knee had a suprapatellar effusion, range of motion 0–70°, no erythema, and no pain with micromotion
left knee had a moderate suprapatellar effusion, range of motion 0–30°, no erythema, and pain with micromotion
peripheral white blood cell count of 12.8×10^3/mm³
C-reactive protein level of 159 mg/L
erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 79 mm/hr
Left knee, 38,580 WBC/mm³, negative gram stain, negative cultures
Right knee, 29,670 WBC/mm³, negative gram stain, negative cultures
onset of pain 12 hours after the injections

concepts.why: The patient presented with acute bilateral knee swelling and pain after viscosupplementation injections, with high synovial fluid white blood cell counts and negative cultures, suggesting an inflammatory reaction to the injections.
The high synovial fluid white blood cell counts could suggest septic arthritis, but the negative gram stains and cultures make this less likely.
The high synovial fluid white blood cell counts could suggest crystal-induced arthritis, but there is no mention of crystal identification in the synovial fluid analysis.
The patient has bilateral knee osteoarthritis, but the acute onset of swelling and pain, along with high synovial fluid white blood cell counts, could suggest an underlying rheumatoid arthritis.
The high synovial fluid white blood cell counts could suggest pseudogout, but there is no mention of crystal identification in the synovial fluid analysis.

rationales.F08: Elevated C-reactive protein level indicates inflammation.
rationales.F09: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate indicates inflammation.
rationales.F10: High white blood cell count in synovial fluid with negative cultures suggests a non-infectious inflammatory process.
rationales.F11: High white blood cell count in synovial fluid with negative cultures suggests a non-infectious inflammatory process.
rationales.F12: Onset of pain after injections suggests a reaction to the viscosupplementation.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of acute bilateral knee swelling and pain, particularly the onset of pain 12 hours after the Synvisc injections, along with the high white blood cell count in the synovial fluid and negative cultures, strongly support this diagnosis.
